prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Monthly mean ozone by monitoring station (language en).
Grid: 13 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Station" · longest unbreakable word 65px · one-line width 65px
  col 2: header "Jan" · longest unbreakable word 27px · one-line width 27px
  col 3: header "Feb" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 4: header "Mar" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 5: header "Apr" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 6: header "May" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 7: header "Jun" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 8: header "Jul" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 9: header "Aug" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 10: header "Sep" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 11: header "Oct" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 12: header "Nov" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 13: header "Dec" · longest unbreakable word 27px · one-line width 27px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 725px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 724px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare monthly mean ozone levels across six monitoring stations, revealing seasonal patterns and station-to-station differences.","reading":"Readers locate a station in column 1, scan horizontally across months within that row, and compare stations vertically within a given month. The month columns form one chronological analytical sequence; the station column is the row key.","groups":["Column 1 (Station): row identifier, should be visually distinct from the data field.","Columns 2–13 (Jan–Dec): one chronological sequence; can be read as quarters Jan–Mar, Apr–Jun, Jul–Sep, Oct–Dec."],"keep_intact":["Station names on one line","Month abbreviations on one line","All numeric values, including decimal points, on one line"],"may_wrap":["None; all cells are short and should remain single-line. Wrapping station names would weaken row identification and scanning."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [90, 52, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 52] · table 725×233px · row heights [33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33] · column headers wrapped 0/13 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [98, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 59] · table 719×233px · row heights [33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33] · column headers wrapped 0/13 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1C: widths [91, 52, 52, 52, 55, 52, 52, 55, 52, 52, 55, 52, 52] · table 725×233px · row heights [33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33] · column headers wrapped 0/13 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0
Constraint adjustments applied: r1B: expected 13 widths; scaled down from 732px to fit 724px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r1A","good":"The month field reads as one continuous chronological band: 52/53px widths are effectively uniform, so nothing in the data area pulls the eye. The station column is visibly the widest and clearly the row key, all cells single-line, row rhythm perfectly even at 33px. Overall a clean, publication-ready grid.","problems":"The proportion between key and data is slightly off. The station column carries 25px of surplus space around a 65px name while each month column has only 3px of surplus around a 28px number, so the names float in air while the numbers sit nearly against the cell borders. The result feels simultaneously loose at the left and cramped across the middle 12 columns — the data field, which is what the reader is actually comparing, is the tightest part of the table.","cause":"Station 90 (65px content) versus months 52 (28px content). The slack was spent on the identifier column, not on the analytical field."},{"design":"r1B","good":"The generous station column (98px) does the most important job well: it separates the row key from the numeric field with a clear band of white space, so a reader never confuses a station name with a data cell. Month grid is calm.","problems":"December is 59px, eight pixels wider than every other month, which invents a false emphasis on the last column and leaves the right edge of the table visibly ragged against the dashed boundary. Meanwhile the remaining months at 51px are the tightest of the three designs, and 5px of the available budget goes unused — the exact 5px that should have been spread across the cramped months instead of dumped into Dec.","cause":"The 8px anomaly at Dec (59 vs 51) plus an over-wide Station at 98; the scaling correction pushed the surplus into the last column rather than distributing it."},{"design":"r1C","good":"Aims at something real — quarter structure in a 12-month sequence — and keeps every cell single-line with a sensible station column at 91px. The base rhythm of 52px is comfortable.","problems":"The quarter idea does not read. Widening Apr, Jul and Oct produces a 3-4px stutter that looks like rounding error or jitter rather than grouping, because the emphasis falls on the first month of each quarter while Jan (also a first month) is not widened — the pattern is internally inconsistent, so the eye finds no rule. Extra space in a centred cell also splits to both sides, so no clean group boundary forms anywhere. The table ends up looking unevenly spaced for no legible reason.","cause":"55px applied to columns 5, 8 and 11 only, breaking the uniform 52px grid asymmetrically."}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"even-key","widths":[96,52,52,52,52,52,52,52,52,52,52,52,52],"change":"Keep r1A's uniform month band but rebalance: station 96 (14px breathing room around the 65px names, enough to read as a distinct key column) and all twelve months at exactly 52px. This removes the 52/53 stutter and stops the identifier column from eating slack that the numeric field needs. Totals 720px, 4px under budget as safety."},{"name":"max-months","widths":[88,53,53,53,53,53,53,53,53,53,53,53,53],"change":"Test the opposite balance: shrink the station column to 88px (just 2px slack beyond the longest name) and give every month 53px, using the full 724px. Twelve equal month columns with 32px of text room make the numbers the most comfortable they can be; the trade-off is a tighter row key. Worth comparing directly against even-key."},{"name":"quarter-end","widths":[90,51,51,56,51,51,56,51,51,56,51,51,56],"change":"Salvage r1C's idea but anchor it correctly: widen only the last month of each quarter (Mar, Jun, Sep, Dec at 56px) so the surplus white space sits between quarters as a soft gutter and never interrupts a quarter. Non-quarter-end months at 51px keep the sequence even, station at 90px stays clearly dominant. Pattern is now internally consistent (4 repeats, one rule) instead of 3 arbitrary bumps."}]}
